modules.summary: The application's core infrastructure, including configuration management, dependency injection, Express app setup, and server startup. Assembles all services, middleware, and routes into a runnable Node.js server.

Handles authentication and authorization using JWT tokens and password hashing. Provides cryptographic password security, token validation middleware, and role-based access control for protecting API endpoints.

Manages per-user shopping carts, allowing customers to add, modify, and retrieve items. Stores cart state in memory as product-to-quantity mappings and validates product availability before additions.

Orchestrates the complete order lifecycle from checkout through fulfillment. Validates inventory, processes payments, creates orders, manages status transitions, and handles cancellations with automatic stock and payment restoration.
Abstracts payment processing through a provider interface with a mock implementation for testing. Enables charging customers and processing refunds without coupling to a specific payment gateway.

Manages the product catalog with inventory tracking, search/filter/sort capabilities, and pagination. Handles stock reservation for orders and release on cancellation, with visibility rules for customers versus admins.

Provides reusable utilities for error handling, HTTP logging, ID generation, input validation, and pagination. Reduces duplication across feature modules through shared middleware and helper functions.

Manages user registration, authentication, and profiles with automatic role assignment and password verification. Provides login/register endpoints and authenticated profile retrieval using JWT tokens.

project.name: express-shop
project.purpose: A full-stack e-commerce backend API built with Express.js that manages products, user accounts, shopping carts, orders, and payments with role-based access control.
project.architecture: The application follows a layered architecture where foundational concerns (data models, utilities, database repositories) feed into service layers that implement business logic, which are then consumed by route handlers and middleware. Entry point src/server.ts starts a Node.js server. The Express app (src/app.ts) registers all routes and middleware. The dependency container (src/container.ts) wires services with their dependencies. Core features are organized by domain: authentication using JWT tokens and password hashing (src/auth); product catalog with inventory tracking and visibility rules (src/products); per-user shopping carts stored in memory (src/cart); order processing that validates inventory, charges customers, and manages status transitions (src/orders); user management with automatic role assignment (src/users); and shared utilities for validation, error handling, logging, and pagination used across modules.
keyConcepts: TypeScript for type safety across the application
JWT authentication with role-based access control
Service layer and repository patterns for data access
Dependency injection container for loose coupling
Order management from checkout to cancellation
Inventory management with stock reservation and restoration
Payment provider abstraction with mock implementation
Input validation, error handling, and pagination utilities
